changes.from: a permanent card paying +1 AP at every Upkeep, at most +2
changes.to: a reusable card: 2 hits to an adjacent non-structure unit, cooldown track position 3, returns to hand; at most 2 held; no AP
Empowered waves for the rest of the game

evidence: RQ-039 and batch_0044: teams that take Dragon win 45-48% and Baron 38-40% on the settled field; the AP a Dragon card pays is inert (P-0009). The lead designer ruled to keep both pits where they are and make the rewards lucrative: Dragon reusable on a short cooldown, Baron permanent because the game is short.
hypothesis: A Dragon card that is a reusable Red Buff pays in tempo, which is the currency the game is short of; a permanent Baron turns one kill into a structural advantage for the rest of the game. Both should raise win rate when secured toward or above 50% and pull teams to the pits.
success_metric: Against batch_0046 (same seed): win rate when Dragon is secured above 50% and when Baron is secured above 55%, and Dragon takes per game up from about 1.4. The objective personality above 45%.
revert_if: Baron secured win rate clears 75% (one kill decides the game), or median length leaves 13-18, or the sieger regains 60%.
side_effects: The Dragon card's hits can kill champions, so kills per game may rise. The AI values the card by simulating its play (T1/T2 choose_card_play), so no weight change is needed; its hold value is zero because it comes back.
note: The Dragon card's effect (2 hits, cooldown 3) is the lab's [DEFAULT] for 'reusable on a short 2-3 round cooldown'; the lead designer named the timing, not the effect. Config: dragon_card {hits 2, cooldown 3}, dragon_ap_each 0, baron_permanent True.

result.verdict: PROVISIONAL - direction right, verdict deferred until games end (tower-HP sweep)

revert_checks.median_length: 20, but the baseline is 20 too (batch_0046): the field does not end games at tower HP 16
revert_checks.sieger_regains_60: 87.9% on the round-20 tiebreak - unreadable until games end

result.reading: Read on a field where every game reaches round 20, so the personality numbers are tiebreak numbers and say nothing yet. What can be read: the reusable Dragon card and permanent Baron move both objectives the right way, and the card's hits show up as 0.34 AP a team-round of wave chips. Re-read on the tower HP the sweep chooses (batch_0048/0049) and with the AREA ruling (P-0012).
